newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Editorials - Oct 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Editorials - Oct 23.

text.p: NOTE: These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted, and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

- With 251 days to go before the British colony reverts to China, editorials in the Hong Kong media concentrated on Chinese dissident Wang Xizhe's intention to join the Kuomintang and the manifesto of Tung Chee-hwa, a contender to become Hong Kong's post-colonial leader.

SING TAO DAILY said Wang should get to know more about Taiwan before making a decision on whether to join the KMT. It said that the combination of increased dealings between mainlanders and Taiwanese, and the Chinese community and the democratic process in Taiwan could make it easier for Wang to promote his political beliefs.

MING PAO DAILY said that under the wave of localisation, "reunification" was seldom mentioned in Taiwan. Taiwan President Li Teng-hui wanted the Kuomintang to be Taiwan's KMT, while Wang, without knowledge of the new political position in Taiwan, wanted to prove that the KMT was China's KMT. It said Wang's theory of using reunification to promote democracy in China was not realistic nnd his political career in Taiwan would not be smooth.

The HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES said that it hoped other chief executive contenders would follow Tung Chee-hwa and Peter Woo and present a detailed political programme. It said Tung's selection manifesto did not go into detail on how he would handle the relationship with Beijing. It said it was questionable whether Hong Kong people would accept his idea of re-establishing traditional Chinese values.
